title: 🧪 Google Builds an “Artificial Internet” to Test AI Agents!
body: 🧪 Google Builds an “Artificial Internet” to Test AI Agents!

Google revealed a project called “Mirror Dimension,” an artificial internet inside the Chrome browser for safely testing automated browsing agents before releasing them to users. The project includes thousands of simulated websites — social networks, online stores, and bank account dashboards — inside a fully isolated environment, with an intercepting proxy, forged certificates, and a multi-agent site coordinator made up of a researcher, a builder, and a critic, and it also tests hidden prompt-injection attacks. Each engineer can test more than 1,000 candidates a day — 30 times manual testing.
Simply put: instead of releasing a smart agent onto the real internet and risking users’ money and data, Google builds a safe, fake copy of the internet to train and test it on.
Would you trust an AI agent to browse the internet on your behalf?
